source_text: Si autem non sustinens reclamantis strepitum veritatis alio tentaris effugere, in plagas incides fortiores. Nam si dicas: Vera quidem est sententia Prophetae, sed in personis grandioribus, quae dicit necessitudines culpis mutuis non gravari, in parvulis autem ab una sui parte mentitur, qua dicit eos reos non esse ob scelera generantium, in alia autem non mentitur, in qua asserit eos nullis parentum virtutibus sublevari, tunc plane foedissimam non disputandi sed confingendi, non eloquendi sed loquendi, non postremo sani hominis, sed excidentis sensu Manichaei libidinem publicabis, si tibi putes contra perspicuam rationem, contra honorem Dei, contra exempla, contra testimonia praeceptorum, contra expositionem iudiciorum, quod libuerit, licere respuere et, quod delectarit, assumere.
pass_a_gloss: But if not sustaining the noise of reclaiming truth you try to flee elsewhere, you will fall into stronger snares. For if you say: True indeed is the sentence of the Prophet, but in greater persons, which says kinships are not burdened by mutual faults, but in little ones it lies from one part of itself, by which it says they are not defendants for the crimes of those generating, but in another it does not lie, in which it asserts they are lifted by no virtues of parents—then plainly you will publicize a most foul appetite not of disputing but of inventing, not of speaking well but of talking, not finally of a sane human but of a Manichaean falling from sense, if you think it is permitted to you against clear reason, against the honor of God, against examples, against the testimonies of precepts, against the exposition of judgments, to spit out what has pleased and to take up what has delighted.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS libido; Blaise often sexual desire; Julian treats as created sensation, not a sin-nature
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS parvulus; Blaise infants without usus rationis

pass_b_english: But if, unable to endure truth’s clamorous protest, you try to escape elsewhere, you will fall into stronger nets. Suppose you say: The prophet’s pronouncement that relatives are not burdened with each other’s faults is indeed true concerning adults; concerning infants, however, it lies in the part saying they are not guilty of their parents’ crimes, but does not lie in the part asserting that they gain no assistance from their parents’ virtues. Then you will openly display a most disgraceful appetite—not for argument but invention, not for eloquence but mere talk, not the appetite of a sane person but of a Manichaean losing his mind. You would be imagining yourself free to reject whatever you please and accept whatever delights you, against plain reason, God’s honor, examples, the testimony of commands, and the explanation of judgments (Ezekiel 18:19–20).

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Explicitly discusses the prophet’s pronouncement on personal righteousness and guilt rather than inherited guilt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
